newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge Q2 edges up on strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge Q2 edges up on strong demand.

text.p: Canadian nickel and copper miner Falconbridge Ltd reported slightly higher second quarter profits on Tuesday while demand for its products was expected to stay strong.
Falconbridge said a major copper project in Chile was now three months ahead of schedule. The Toronto-based company also forecast a balanced world nickel market this year and a surplus in 1998.

"We think we had a reasonably good quarter in the second quarter of this year. Production was quite good and operating costs continued to trend downwards and demand for all our metals are quite strong," Falconbridge President and Chief Executive Oyvind Hushovd said in a conference call with analysts.
The company reported net income of C$60.3 million in quarter ended June 30, up slightly from C$59 million in the same period a year ago.
Per share earnings were flat at C$0.33 per share. Net income was 31 percent higher than the first quarter of 1997.
"Although they met my expectations, I actually thought they did a little bit better than what people in average were thinking," said David Kellar, an analyst with Griffiths McBurney & Partners.
Falconbridge said the results reflected good demand and improved copper and zinc prices. Nickel prices were pressured by higher Russian exports of primary nickel and nickel-bearing scrap.
Joe Laezza, vice-president of marketing and sales, predicted a balanced world nickel market in 1997, followed by a surplus in 1998.
"A lot of it will depend on what Russia will be doing. It's a very preliminary number, but we are looking at a surplus next year of about 13,000 tonnes with some assumptions," Laezza said.
Analysts said if Falconbridge's prediction is correct, a surplus would not bode well for nickel prices.
Meanwhile, Falconbridge said its US$1.76 billion Collahuasi copper property in northern Chile is now expected to start production in October 1998, about three months ahead of schedule and on budget.
The company also said it expected the project to produce 330,000 tonnes in 1999. Some analysts had expected smaller output from Collahuasi in its first full year of production.
"That is a piece of good news because as we get closer to the start-up date the stock should start to respond," Kellar said.
Falconbridge's stock slipped 0.05 at 25.65 in afternoon turnover of 281,700 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. The stock hit a 52-week low of 25.30 earlier in the session.
The Raglan nickel mine in Quebec is still expected to produce concentrate in December, nearly three months ahead of plan.
But Raglan's C$486 million pricetag may climb by 10 percent due to higher construction and concentrate handling costs, said chief financial officer Lars-Eric Johansson.
The company said it was hopeful a new labor agreement can be reached with 1,400 unionized mine workers at its Sudbury, Ontario operations.
The current contract expires on August 1, 1997.
Falconbridge produced 42,100 tonnes of nickel in Sudbury last year, along with 48,800 tonnes of copper and 730 tonnes of cobalt.
